solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fish dish containing potassium

indicators.note: containing tells us the dish holds the next item inside it

blocks.note: a pie is a baked dish
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A fish dish with potassium in it, as on a nutrition label.
explanation.definitionFit: The pike is a long predatory freshwater species with sharp teeth, caught by anglers.

clue.text: Job with Head of Alsace Resistance after VE Day?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so we keep only the start of Alsace

blocks.note: a post is a job or position
W is the standard abbreviation for with
first letter of Alsace
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A wartime job with the leader of the Alsace Resistance, taken up once Europe was liberated.
explanation.walkthrough: The French Resistance flavour hides that Resistance is simply R, as in physics; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: VE Day marked victory in Europe in 1945, so anything after it belongs to the period following the Second World War.

clue.text: Flipping obsessive expert, one high in stature, smart Alec

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it back to front, so the expert's word is read backwards

blocks.note: a wonk is a person obsessively devoted to a specialist subject
I is the Roman numeral one
someone tall is high in stature

explanation.surface: A grumble about an obsessive expert who is tall and a smart Alec to boot.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping reads like a mild British oath, not an instruction to reverse the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart Alec is a cocky person who thinks they have every answer, which is exactly this label.

clue.text: Renouncing a bitcoin ad that’s circulating

indicators.note: letters that are circulating move around and settle in a new order

blocks.note: all ten letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone giving up on cryptocurrency because of a bitcoin advert doing the rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Formally giving up a throne or responsibility is the act of renunciation, a noun matching the gerund.

clue.text: Wine store putting up mature old Burgundy principally

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up makes it read from the bottom upwards
principally points to the principal, leading letter of Burgundy

blocks.note: mature wine has aged
O is the usual abbreviation for old
first letter of Burgundy

explanation.surface: A wine shop laying down mature old Burgundy for the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: Putting up wine sounds like storing it, but here it reverses the pieces in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish cellar or shop where wine is kept and sold.

clue.text: The setter’s visibly embarrassed to admit papa, behold, was begging

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the next pieces go inside

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself as I, so the setter's is I'M
an embarrassed face turns red
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet
lo is an old word for behold

explanation.surface: The setter blushes, owning up that Dad saw him pleading.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to ask desperately, so the past tense means someone was pleading earnestly.

clue.text: Ready for a fight by obelisks, with honours even

blocks.note: by and at both mean next to, as in by the door
an obelisk is also the printer's dagger mark
with honours even a match is drawn

explanation.surface: Two rivals standing by monuments with the contest still level.
explanation.walkthrough: Obelisks look like stone monuments, but printers call the dagger symbol an obelisk too.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for two parties in open hostility, poised to attack each other.

clue.text: Parliament rising to support Ireland’s premier epic work of literature

indicators.note: the premier letter is the first one of Ireland
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: first letter of Ireland
the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: Irish parliament standing up for the country's leading work of literature.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, to support means to sit beneath, so the reversed parliament goes under the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem of the Trojan War is one of the great founding epics of Western literature.

clue.text: Dark edges of intimate clothing

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters at each end

blocks.note: night is the dark part of the day
outer letters of intimate

explanation.surface: A dark-edged piece of lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a garment worn in bed, so it is an item of clothing given by example.

clue.text: San Marino ready for manufacturing salt

indicators.note: manufacturing makes something new from raw materials, so these letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: all fourteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: The little republic of San Marino gears up to produce salt.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt looks like the industrial product, but an old salt is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is informal for an experienced sailor, and an ordinary seaman is a junior naval rating.

clue.text: That is The Times boss purged

blocks.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for that is or namely
a Times setter calls the paper our own
the boss of a newspaper is its editor, ED

explanation.surface: The editor of The Times sacked staff in a clear-out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as the setter speaking, The Times boss is our editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to clean thoroughly or clear out, so a purged place has been scoured.

clue.text: Page including verbiage

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page
including something is adding it

explanation.surface: A page stuffed with wordiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding is superfluous material added to fill out a text, which is wordy excess.

clue.text: Barking “woof!”, dog tiring at play

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters are thrown into crazy disorder

blocks.note: all fifteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A dog barking woof, worn out from playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the dog's noise but is the slang for mad; play is the definition, not the dog's game.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett's absurdist drama in which two tramps wait in vain is a famous stage work.

clue.text: Former leader emerging from Korea gang

indicators.note: something emerging from these words is already sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An ex-ruler coming out of a Korean gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth President of the United States, so a past head of state.

clue.text: Say a reverend bishop popped round to guzzle energy drink?

indicators.note: turned round, the pieces are read in the opposite direction
guzzling takes something in, so the next letter goes inside

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
taken as written
Rev is the abbreviation for reverend
B is the chess notation for bishop
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A vicar and a bishop dropping in for an energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Energy drink reads as one item, but the definition is only drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any liquid for drinking other than water, so a general word for something to drink.

clue.text: Higher class work performed by tree surgeon?

blocks.note: first meaning: superior to others
second meaning, taken literally: a tree surgeon trims branches overhead

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading of the idiom as an arborist's overhead chop.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means noticeably superior, while a tree surgeon literally saws into branches overhead.

clue.text: Riverbank creature having earth in Buddhist temple

indicators.note: in places the earth inside the temple

blocks.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
terra is Latin for earth

explanation.surface: An animal by the river with its earth set inside a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty, the water vole in The Wind in the Willows, lives on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The water vole, popularly called by this name, burrows into banks of rivers and streams.

clue.text: Backing singer of swing, Yankee jazz fan and wild thing

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the singer's name runs backwards

blocks.note: Ella Fitzgerald was a great swing and jazz singer
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
cat is old jazz slang for a fan or musician

explanation.surface: A band line-up: backing vocalist, an American jazz fan and a wild one.
explanation.walkthrough: Backing singer reads as a single role, but backing is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray urban feline living rough in the streets is untamed, so a feral animal.

clue.text: Light rubber and aluminium device extending PC performance

blocks.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
an add-in is software that extends a computer program

explanation.surface: A light eraser and an aluminium gadget to speed up your computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Light rubber looks like a soft eraser; it is the man who rubbed a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale the hero rubs a magic lamp and releases a genie.

clue.text: Sharp expressions of disapproval about being stuck in A&E

indicators.note: turned about, the sounds of disapproval are read backwards
stuck in means placed inside the next item

blocks.note: A and E are kept as written
tut is a click of the tongue showing disapproval

explanation.surface: Sharp tutting from patients stuck waiting in A&E.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharp is shrewd and quick-witted, which is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Always empty eateries on top of Table Mountain

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outer letters
the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: ever means always
outer letters of eateries
first letter of Table

explanation.surface: Restaurants on Cape Town's Table Mountain are always empty.
explanation.walkthrough: Table Mountain is a real South African peak, but only Mountain is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest peak, in the Himalayas on the Nepal–Tibet border, is an example of a summit.

clue.text: Second in command collecting junk still

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the junk is held inside

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
i/c is short for in charge or in command
tat is cheap worthless stuff

explanation.surface: A deputy commander hoarding junk and refusing to throw it away.
explanation.walkthrough: Second in command reads as one deputy, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Static describes something not moving, matching still as an adjective meaning motionless.

clue.text: A true Damascene conversion holding mass in leisure centre

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so the extra letter joins the mix
a conversion changes something into a new form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: fourteen letters used as fodder
M is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: Someone has a road-to-Damascus conversion while going to Mass at a leisure centre.
explanation.walkthrough: A Damascene conversion is a sudden change of heart, after St Paul on the road to Damascus.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall full of slot machines and video games is a place people go for fun and leisure.

clue.text: Take command of moneylending business, assuming power for years

indicators.note: assuming here means taking on one letter in place of another

blocks.note: usury is lending money at interest
P is the symbol for power
Y is the abbreviation for years; this is the letter swapped out

explanation.surface: A loan shark builds up power over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: Power for years means P replaces Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize a position or authority without right, so to grab control of it.

clue.text: Percussionist daughter getting increasingly weird

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
rum is British slang for odd, so rummer is odder

explanation.surface: A parent notes their musician daughter is getting stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum, meaning odd or peculiar, is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the kit of skins and cymbals in a band is a percussion player.

clue.text: Robust line in figurative expression that hurts

indicators.note: in places the cry of pain inside the figure of speech

blocks.note: a trope is a figure of speech
ow is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: A tough line within a painful metaphor.
explanation.walkthrough: Line looks like a line of text, matching figurative expression, but it is a cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong cable used to haul a vehicle is a sturdy cord, which is a line in nautical terms.

clue.text: Knife work unfortunately put Dan in prison

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order
in places the jumbled letters inside the prison

blocks.note: nick is British slang for a prison or police station
the six letters of put Dan rearranged

explanation.surface: Dan was jailed for knife crime, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Knife work sounds criminal, but it is cosmetic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal for cosmetic surgery, where a surgeon's scalpel tightens the skin.

clue.text: Turning tap to conserve key non-renewable fuel

indicators.note: turning it round makes the word run the other way
conserving means keeping something safe inside

blocks.note: taken as written
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Turning off the tap to save a key fossil fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Peat forms over thousands of years, so it is treated as non-renewable.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly decayed bog vegetation is dug and burnt for heat, and it regenerates far too slowly to replace.
